_note: Every rate here is copied from an official page, never computed and never estimated. Each section carries its own source URL and the date it was checked. Re-check the source before changing a number, and update _checked_at when you do. The last rate that was inlined in code on this machine came out 18x wrong because the model had changed underneath it.

stt._note: Quoted: $0.04 per hour, and "Minimum billed length: 10 seconds. If you submit a request less than this, you will still be billed for 10 seconds." Duration is taken from Groq's own verbose_json response, not measured locally — they bill on what they report.

tts._note: Quoted for Chirp 3: HD voices: "0 to 1 million characters | US$0.00003 per character (US$30 per 1 million characters)". The same page states the billed count includes spaces and newlines, and all SSML tags except <mark>. NOTE: the page's free-allowance wording names WaveNet (1M) and Standard (4M) only; it does NOT name Chirp 3 HD, and the Chirp 3 HD row bills from character 0. No free allowance is assumed here — assuming one would silently under-count the budget.
